item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Mike and Katy are planning a day trip for their class.

They plan to go from their school in Ourtown to one of the towns of Acton, Burley, Camford, or Darley.

[Image: Map of Ourtown and surrounding towns]

descriptors: Acton – Yes; Burley – No; Darley - Yes
Other Incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.figure_description:
A map enclosed in a wavy rectangular border, labeled "Map drawn to scale" in the bottom-left corner. Five locations are marked with solid black dots and labels:
- "Ourtown" is located in the lower-middle portion of the map.
- "Acton" is northwest of Ourtown, connected to Ourtown by a straight path line.
- "Burley" is directly north of Acton, connected to Acton by a vertical straight path line.
- "Camford" is northeast of Ourtown, connected to Ourtown by a straight path line.
- "Darley" is southeast of Ourtown, connected to Ourtown by a straight path line.
There are three clusters of small stylized pine tree symbols: one cluster between the path to Acton and the path to Camford, one cluster west of Ourtown, and one cluster southeast of Ourtown between the paths to Camford and Darley.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.
